text:
Winnipeg won 5-2 on a night when the chances were closer than the scoreboard. WPG's expected goals edge was 2.82 to 2.49, and a replay of every shot gives them the win only 56 percent of the time. The gap came in goal. Calvin Pickard allowed 2.2 more goals than the 25 shots he faced should have cost MIN, while Stuart Skinner stopped 19 of 21 for 0.49 goals saved above expected.

The first period belonged to MIN on chances, 1.53 expected goals to 0.82, and it still ended 2-2. Cole Perfetti opened the scoring 1:50 in on a tip-in worth a 4 percent chance, the least likely goal of the night. Kirill Kaprizov answered twice, the second a tip-in 44 seconds after Mark Scheifele's snap shot made it 2-1, to level things going into the break.

WPG took over from there. They out-chanced MIN 1.58 to 0.58 in the second, and Perfetti's power-play snap shot with 3:24 left in the period made it 3-2. Kyle Connor added a wrist shot 4:06 into the third and Cole Koepke another at 14:42. Scheifele finished with a goal and two assists, and Neal Pionk had two assists in 23:48. MIN's best late look, a 25 percent chance for Bobby Brink, ended in Skinner's glove, and Kaprizov's two goals were all the visitors had to show for it.
